properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 3:38AM MST until October 25 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST tonight /100 AM MDT Sunday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is imminent or
occurring. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 333 AM MST /433 AM MDT/, water levels have crested at Winslow
and are expected to fall through the day today. However,
downstream impacts will continue at Birdsprings through at least
this evening.
- For the Little Colorado River at Winslow:
At 3:00am MST /4:00am MDT/ the stage was 18.11 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels are expected forecast to fall below action
stage around 10:00am MST /11:00am MDT/ today.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise, Bushman Acres, Homolovi Ruins State
Park and Clear Creek Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of rivers are unstable and
unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous. Do not attempt to cross
flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 11:31AM MDT until October 25 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

San Juan River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Farmington.

* WHEN...From this morning to Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.5 feet, Overbank flow is occurring from just below
the confluence of the Animas and San Juan Rivers at Farmington, and
continuing downriver through Shiprock. At this water level, the
fast flow can result in river bank erosion but otherwise minor
flood damage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 5.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 7.2 feet
late tomorrow evening.
- Action stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 11:30AM MDT until October 25 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

San Juan River At Shiprock affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Shiprock.

* WHEN...From this morning to Sunday afternoon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 12.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall to 12.0 feet this afternoon. It
will then rise to 12.5 feet this evening. It will fall to 11.9
feet just after midnight tonight. It will then rise to 14.2 feet
Saturday morning. It will fall again and remain below flood
stage.
- Action stage is 13.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 11:29AM MDT until October 24 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Animas River Near Cedar Hill affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Animas River near Cedar Hill.

* WHEN...From this morning to Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 9.5 feet, Minor overbank flooding of low spots along
the river from the New Mexico-Colorado border down to the riverwalk
in Farmington can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 7.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.8 feet
tomorrow afternoon.
- Action stage is 9.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 11:28AM MDT until October 24 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Watch for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Animas River At Farmington affecting Northwest Plateau zone.

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...Animas River at Farmington.

* WHEN...From Friday evening to Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Portions of the riverwalk in Farmington are
flooded. Local overbank flooding is occurring along the lower
Animas River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 6.4 feet.
- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached late tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you are in the watch area, remain alert to possible flooding.

Residents and those with interests near the river should monitor
rising water levels and be prepared for possible Flood Warnings.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon MDT.
